title: Chapter 37: Expansion
html:
The combination of Chen Ge’s costume, his expression, and that question was enough to make Brother Feng wonder whether the Haunted House proprietor was stranger than the attraction itself.

“Relax. I’m joking.” Chen Ge was a little disappointed. He had asked because Brother Feng had shown unusual resilience. With only a small interruption from the doll, he had broken the mirror’s influence and remained aware enough to resist it.

That was exactly the sort of composure Chen Ge valued. He had briefly considered asking Brother Feng for help with future supernatural problems, but the student was clearly in no condition to entertain the idea.

Looks like I’m handling this one myself.Chen Ge locked the Murder by Midnight scenario and helped Brother Feng downstairs. Halfway down, the black phone vibrated. He immediately checked it, expecting more bad news.

“Monthly visitors exceeded 100. Positive reputation: 60%. Expansion requirements met.”

“Each Haunted House expansion grants one mysterious reward. After three expansions, the Haunted House will upgrade to a Maze of Terror.”

I can expand already?Expansion was good news, but it was not Chen Ge’s immediate priority. First he had to deal with the thing in the mirrors.

Outside, bright sunlight washed over the steps. The Jiujiang Medical University students were gathered in a miserable-looking cluster, recovering in various states of embarrassment and exhaustion.

The scene gave Chen Ge a strong sense of déjà vu, only on a much larger scale. Forty minutes earlier they had marched in like a small expeditionary force. Now none of them looked eager to discuss their performance.

Nearby visitors whispered and pointed, but Chen Ge was not overly concerned. A House of Horrors was supposed to leave an impression.

He helped Brother Feng join the rest of the group, completing the collection.

“Xiao Chen! Over here.” The crowd had attracted Uncle Xu again. The middle-aged man looked caught between exasperation and disbelief. “Explain this. Last time one visitor fainted. Today you have seven university students sitting outside like they just survived a disaster. Are you trying to put this park on the news?”

Chen Ge cleared his throat. “They paid for the Haunted House experience, and I gave them an excellent Haunted House experience. I also followed the attraction rules, and the security footage can confirm that the performers never made unsafe physical contact.”

“Then what happened to the bump on that girl’s head?” Uncle Xu asked quietly, nodding toward Xiao Hui.

“That was an accident inside one of the rooms. She hid in a cupboard, got startled, and bumped into the back panel. I stopped the scenario and brought her out as soon as it happened.” For once, Chen Ge omitted the theatrical embellishments.

“So you’re saying it was bad luck?”

“An unfortunate accident, yes.”

“Stop treating safety like a punch line. You need to be more careful and make sure this doesn’t happen again,” Uncle Xu said with a sigh. “One serious accident or one angry customer could damage the Haunted House permanently.”

“I know. I’ll be more careful.” Chen Ge did not argue, although his thoughts were considerably less obedient.Fine. Safety first. But I’m still keeping a few surprises for anyone who comes looking for trouble.

Uncle Xu studied him and clearly doubted how much of the lecture had actually landed. “Xiao Chen, I know I’m not your parent, but there are things someone needs to say now that yours aren’t here.”

“I’m listening.”

“Xu Wan told me you were on the news this morning. She said you were the witness who helped the police make progress on that old fire case.” Uncle Xu did not look pleased.

“That was me.”

“Then what were you doing at a place like that in the middle of the night? Do you understand how dangerous the situation became?” Uncle Xu did not give him room to joke. “If money is tight, there are other solutions. I can help you deal with what you owe the park for now. You’re still young. Don’t trade your safety for a reward.”

“Don’t worry, Uncle Xu. I know.”

“I hope you do. If that’s everything, I’m going back to work. And get those students off the steps soon—having them sprawled outside the attraction isn’t a great advertisement.” Uncle Xu turned to leave, but Chen Ge stopped him. “What now?”

“I actually do need one favor,” Chen Ge admitted. “Could you lend me five thousand yuan? I want to install more cameras throughout the Haunted House. I’ll pay you back as soon as the reward money arrives.”

After the incidents involving He San and He Feng, better monitoring no longer felt optional. The attraction had too many blind spots.

“You still want to invest more money in this place?” Uncle Xu stopped. “I can lend it to you, but I’m going to be honest: the park itself is struggling. Investing here right now could mean throwing money into a sinking business.”

He led Chen Ge into the shade before continuing. “New Century Park has been open for eleven years, and most of its major attractions are dated. Visitors want newer technology, stronger themes, and experiences they can’t get elsewhere. We’re falling behind. Aside from your Haunted House, attendance at nearly every attraction has been declining.”

“I know.” Chen Ge had already decided that improving the Haunted House’s safety and operations came first.

“You don’t know the whole situation.” Uncle Xu lowered his walkie-talkie. “The Virtual Reality Futuristic Carnival in eastern Jiujiang is nearly finished. Once it opens, it’ll be one of the newest major amusement parks in the region. People here can see what’s coming. From management down to maintenance staff, everyone is wondering what they’ll do if attendance keeps falling. You’re the only person still trying to expand.”
